source_text.Q-1054: MEDIUM, R1 from ISS-1042 follow_ups (SECURITY-REVIEWER F2), supervisor-assigned 2026-10-12. Queue Q-1054 / GH #2400, issue_ref ISS-1054. See task.description.

task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 hard gate (.claude/agents/code-design-validator.md) on the ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis and fix design for RC-E (Q-1087 / GH #2448): DIAG blocks of simultaneously firing partition watchdogs interleave mid-line on stderr. Design: handoffs/WF03-RCEDIAGINTERLEAVE-20261013/step-01-issue-fixer.json (read result in full). Branch feature/WF03-RCEDIAGINTERLEAVE-20261013, local only, do not push.
IMPORTANT: the fix changes scripts/test_parallel.sh, the partition runner EVERY backend CI shard uses; a regression reddens every PR. Be strict. The previous round (Q-1053) found 4 MAJOR issues in the design at this gate; expect to find real ones.
Validate independently (read the script and test files yourself; do not trust the report): (1) mechanism: is "sed flushes 4096-byte chunks at arbitrary offsets to a shared pipe" really the cause (check the byte arithmetic against the CI log lines quoted in the handoff; gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow/actions/jobs/<id>/logs for jobs 114960028887, 114986157916, 115074477292); is a single `cat file >&2` write truly one write(2) and atomic enough for a pipe when the file is larger than PIPE_BUF (4096): POSIX guarantees atomicity only up to PIPE_BUF for pipes; the block is ~13.4 KB. State clearly what is guaranteed on Linux for a >PIPE_BUF write to a pipe with several concurrent writers (it is NOT atomic in general; the lock is then what serialises), and what happens when stderr is a file (O_APPEND or not). Does the design rely on the lock for correctness and on cat only for fewer syscalls? Is the "emit anyway after ~3 s" fallback acceptable, and does it reintroduce the interleave only in the degenerate case? (2) the lock: mkdir spin, bounded; stale lock after a SIGKILLed holder; release on every path including `set -u`/errexit and TERM; nested runner invocations sharing the tmp dir name; interaction with the existing diag-host.lock; the EXIT trap rm -rf of tmp_dir (BASHPID guard from Q-1053 must still hold: the watchdog subshell must not remove the tmp dir); time budget: the watchdog sends TERM after the DIAG; worst-case added latency for N partitions x 3 s lock waits; does it break TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S semantics or the asserted `elapsed < t+15` in test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs; (3) the regression tests T1..T3 (sed shim with a file barrier, mkdir shim, rmdir shim): deterministic, fail on the unfixed script, pass on the fixed, no wall-clock windows of their own, async false, no leaks, follow test/scripts/test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs and test/support/test_parallel_capture.ex conventions, bash 5.1/5.2 on Linux CI and Windows git-bash host; does the barrier shim risk hanging (bounded?); (4) mutant list adequacy, and the non-killable M2 (variable + printf): is it really non-killable, would a stricter assertion kill it; (5) baseline/stress plan: loop shape, iteration counts, statistical meaning (P(0 failures)=0.94^N), mutex discipline, cap ~40 min; (6) any other concurrent multi-line emitter missed; (7) unambiguous enough for a weak model: the exact ELIXIR-DEV order and the mandatory local verification list (all test_parallel_* test files, fail-first, mutants, bash -n, shellcheck if present, format, check.static, check_async_sandbox_reachability, lint_handoffs, one end-to-end real-runner slice). No mix is needed for this step; if you must, use the machine mutex: L=/c/Users/tvolo/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/mixlock; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$L")"; until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 20; done; trap 'rmdir "$L" 2>/dev/null' EXIT; cd /c/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow && MIX_ENV=test <ONE mix invocation>. Container experiments ok (throwaway, remove after). Foreground only; no Monitors. Verdict PASS/FAIL (BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR with mechanical corrections numbered G1..Gn). Result into your handoff (COMPLETED, result.status, no BOM, LF, artifacts_out under result, no self-reference); commit locally, no push. Message ends: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. TIME BOX: report within ~20 minutes; a push deadline is near.

result.summary: FAIL (no partial credit): mechanism and fix direction CONFIRMED, but the design as written has 6 MAJOR spec/test defects (G1-G6) and 5 MINOR (G7-G11) that must be corrected before ELIXIR-DEV. None needs a new experiment; every correction is mechanical. The root-cause diagnosis (sed 4096-byte stdio flush mid-line on a pipe shared by 3 watchdog subshells) is correct and independently re-derived; the temp-file + single cat emitter is the right fix.

independent_verification.mechanism: CONFIRMED. gh api logs of job 114960028887 re-read: `test_parallel: DIAG partition 3:   P3-199974-` + 19 L, immediately followed by `test_parallel: DIAG partition 2:   P2-199962-` + a full 300-col line (total 399 = 64 + 35 + 300). Arithmetic re-derived from the stub: tail -n 40 = 39 long lines P-199962..P-200000 + the `....` line; P-199974 is the 13th, preceded by 12 x (35 prefix + 300 + LF = 336) = 4032 B; 35 + 10 + 19 = 64; 4032 + 64 = 4096 exactly = the glibc 4096 B stdio buffer of GNU sed with stdout a pipe (sed flushes per line only with -u or a non-stdout fp). The `echo` header is a separate builtin write and does not shift sed's buffer. The block is 39*336 + 40 + header/approx/running lines ~ 13.3 KB, so sed does 3 flushes + a final one; the `marked` case (< 4096 B) flushes once and cannot show it. Other partition's flush landing between two flushes of this partition = observed corruption. Not a harness splitter and not O_APPEND.
independent_verification.atomicity_statement_required_in_design: POSIX guarantees atomicity ONLY for write(2) <= PIPE_BUF (4096) to a pipe. A ~13.3 KB write is NOT guaranteed atomic by any standard. On Linux pipe_write copies under pipe->mutex and only drops it (sleeps) when the pipe is full (default capacity 64 KB = 16 pages), so a 13.3 KB write onto a pipe with >= 13.3 KB free is contiguous in practice (3 blocks = 40 KB < 64 KB; measured 0/100 corrupt). If the pipe lacks space (reader stalled), the writer blocks mid-write with the mutex released and another writer (a WARNING echo, a job-control notice, a fall-through emitter) can land at a page boundary inside the block, i.e. mid-line. For a regular file as stderr: all writers inherit ONE open file description, so each write(2) is serialised by the f_pos lock (Linux >= 3.14) and appended in full; with O_APPEND likewise atomic; with separately opened non-O_APPEND descriptions writes would overwrite each other (not the case here: the description is inherited). So correctness rests PRIMARILY on the single write(2) (cat with a 128 KiB buffer on coreutils >= 8.x; busybox cat equivalent) PLUS the pipe having free space; the mkdir lock is defence in depth that serialises cooperating emitters even when a write blocks on a full pipe. The 3 s fall-through is acceptable (still one write; only a holder blocked > 3 s on a full pipe, i.e. a stalled reader, lets a second emitter overlap) but the design must say this, not 'the lock serialises'.
independent_verification.set_u_hazard_reproduced: Reproduced on bash 5.2.37: under `set -u`, `f(){ [ "$got" = 1 ] && echo y; return 0; }; ( f; echo after )` prints `got: unbound variable` and the subshell EXITS before `echo after`. The watchdog runs `test_parallel_watchdog_diag` inside `( ... ) &` under the script's `set -u`; an uninitialised `got` on the lock-not-obtained path kills the watchdog subshell before `kill -TERM` => hung partition never killed (the exact RC-C class of harm). The design's helper text never initialises `got`.
independent_verification.shim_exec_semantics: Verified bash 5.2: `PATH="$REAL_PATH" exec sed "$@"` inside a PATH shim resolves the real sed (no exec loop). Bash 5.1 same semantics.
independent_verification.stats: 0.94^40 = 0.084, 0.94^50 = 0.045: arithmetic correct. Caveat accepted: the Windows git-bash host has different pipe/stdio semantics, a 0/40 baseline there is expected and is NOT evidence; the deterministic shim test is the real regression guard.

findings.defect: `got` is never initialised. Under the script's `set -u` the not-obtained path (`[ "$got" = 1 ]`) aborts the WATCHDOG SUBSHELL before the TERM (reproduced). Design also does not state `local` for loop counter/`got`.
findings.correction: Specify the helper's first statement as `local blockfile="$1" got=0 n=0` and the release as `if [ "$got" -eq 1 ]; then rmdir -- "$tmp_dir/diag-emit.lock" 2>/dev/null; fi` (never `[ ... ] && rmdir` as a last statement), function ends with explicit `return 0`. State: every variable the helper and watchdog function read is initialised before first use (the whole script runs under `set -u`, and the helper runs inside a `( )` watchdog whose death means no TERM).

findings.defect: Wrong counts. The helper is called for the 3 partition blocks AND the host block (design says the host block uses the same helper), i.e. 4 emits. With the mkdir shim denying every attempt and 30 tries per emit, mkdir-denied appears 30 x 4 = 120 times, not 'exactly 3'; test_3 sees exactly 4 lock rmdirs, not 3. A faithful implementor writes a red-on-green test.
findings.correction: test_2: assert `count(mkdir-denied) == 4 * 30` (name the constant @lock_tries 30 in the test with a comment that it mirrors the helper), status == 1, all 3 blocks + 1 host block intact, no extra wall-clock bound beyond the existing run limit (30 shim forks x 2 sequential emits is slow on git-bash; do NOT reuse `elapsed < (t+15)*1000` here). test_3: assert exactly 4 `rmdir .../diag-emit.lock` log entries. M3 'killed by' becomes: test_2 count == 120 fails with 0 (killed behaviourally, not merely 'presence').

findings.defect: run_until_premise reruns the script up to 3 times with escalating t using a FIXED extra_env list. A STUB_BARRIER / STUB_LOG path computed once per test is shared by the attempts: stale barrier files from attempt 1 satisfy the '>= 3 files .k' condition instantly in attempt 2 (lock-step lost, T1 no longer red on the unfixed script), the non-vacuity check '>= 3 *.1 files' passes on leftovers, and mkdir-denied/rmdir counts accumulate across attempts (G2 counts wrong after any retry).
findings.correction: run_script/3 must create the per-attempt state itself: `state = Path.join(tmp, "shimstate"); File.mkdir_p!(Path.join(state, "barrier"))` and add `{"STUB_BARRIER", Path.join(state, "barrier")}` and `{"STUB_LOG", Path.join(state, "calls.log")}` to its env (tmp there is already the per-attempt `attempt-<t>` directory). Counting helpers read the LAST attempt's state only. Never pass barrier/log paths through the caller's extra_env.

findings.where: regression_test_design shims (sed, mkdir, rmdir) in write_stubs
findings.defect: (a) The sed shim is installed in stubbin for EVERY test of the file but, as specified, its chunk/barrier branch is keyed only on the first argument; the existing 'marked'/'huge'/'quick' tests would pass through the barrier path (or `read -N ""` with an empty STUB_SED_CHUNK) unless gated. (b) It only intercepts when `$1` starts with `s/^/test_parallel: DIAG partition `, so M8 (`sed -u "s/^/..."`, or `stdbuf -oL sed ...`) is NOT intercepted (first arg is `-u`) and M8 is not deterministically killed as claimed. (c) `REAL_PATH via env` taken from Elixir `System.get_env("PATH")` is a Windows-format list on the git-bash host; the in-bash PATH differs.
findings.correction: (a) Each shim begins `[ -n "${STUB_SED_CHUNK:-}" ] || { PATH="$REAL_PATH" exec sed "$@"; }` (mkdir/rmdir shims: `[ -n "${STUB_LOG:-}" ]`-style gating on their own env var, pass-through otherwise) so every existing test is byte-for-byte unaffected. (b) The sed shim scans ALL arguments (`for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in 's/^/test_parallel: DIAG partition '*) part=...; break;; esac; done`), not only `$1`. (c) The launcher string in run_script exports the in-bash value before prefixing: `REAL_PATH="$PATH"; export REAL_PATH; d=$(cygpath -u "$1" ...); PATH="$d:$PATH"` (pass-through then does `PATH="$REAL_PATH" exec <tool> "$@"`).

findings.defect: `sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || sleep 1` makes the 'hard ~3 s cap by iteration count' false: where fractional sleep is unsupported every iteration sleeps 1 s => 30 s before the TERM, which also exceeds the harness `elapsed` budgets. The script already requires fractional sleep unguarded (lines 569 `sleep 0.05`, 685 `sleep 0.2`), so the fallback adds risk, not portability.
findings.correction: Delete the `|| sleep 1` fallback: loop body is `mkdir "$tmp_dir/diag-emit.lock" 2>/dev/null && { got=1; break; }; n=$((n + 1)); sleep 0.1`, `while [ "$n" -lt 30 ]`. State in the script comment: worst case ~3 s of sleeping plus fork time (about 5 s on loaded git-bash), the bound is an iteration count, not wall clock, and stale lock costs each emit that long (partition emit then host emit, sequential => up to ~2 x bound before the TERM; still < the harness `elapsed < t+15` on Linux).

findings.where: design completeness for weak-model execution (task item 7)
findings.defect: The design has prose and a routing line but NO exact ELIXIR-DEV step order and NO mandatory local-verification list, no statement of where the helper is defined relative to test_parallel_diag_t/_run (it must precede first use and be defined before the watchdog function is CALLED, in the same top-level region), no statement that no new TEST_* knob may be introduced (test_parallel_env_test.exs greps the script for every `${TEST_...` read and fails when TestParallelEnv does not list it), and no instruction to update the test moduledoc case list.
findings.correction: Add this ordered list to fix_design: (1) write the regression tests + shims first (T1..T3, helper assert_blocks_intact, leak/cat-shim assertions of G8); (2) run the new tests against the UNMODIFIED script and record: T1 RED (barrier-forced interleave), T2/T3 RED (no lock exists: 0 denials / 0 rmdirs); (3) implement helper `test_parallel_diag_emit` placed immediately above `test_parallel_watchdog_diag`, change the two emitters to assemble-to-file-then-emit (partition block to `$tmp_dir/diag-block-$idx.txt`, host block to `$tmp_dir/diag-host-block.txt`), constants literal (30 tries, 0.1 s), NO new TEST_* knob; (4) `bash -n scripts/test_parallel.sh`; `shellcheck scripts/test_parallel.sh` only if installed (it is NOT installed on the host: record 'not available'); (5) mix format --check-formatted; (6) ONE mix invocation under the machine mutex running ALL of: test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs, test_parallel_watchdog_orphan_test.exs, test_parallel_race_regression_test.exs, test_parallel_instrumentation_test.exs, test_parallel_shard_test.exs, test_parallel_env_test.exs, test_parallel_env_guard_test.exs, and the three test_parallel_*_test.sh via their own runners; (7) mutants M1..M8 + the G8 mutants, each: apply, run the single killing test, quote RED, revert (git diff clean after); kill orphan bash/sleep afterwards (G10); (8) one end-to-end real-runner slice: `TEST_PARALLEL_N=2 scripts/test_parallel.sh test/scripts/test_parallel_env_test.exs` (exit 0, `2/2 partitions reported`); (9) `mix letflow.check.static`; `mix letflow.check_async_sandbox_reachability`; `mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir <own handoff>`; `mix letflow.check_boundaries`; `mix letflow.check_issue_refs`; (10) update the moduledoc case list (new cases 4-6) and add the script header paragraph naming RC-E, the single-write rationale and the atomicity statement (G9); (11) commit locally, no push.

findings.defect: Assembly into a file replaces streaming emission. If the file cannot be created or written (tmp_dir removed under the watchdog: the RC-A shape; or ENOSPC, exactly the host condition a hung-partition DIAG exists to report) the old code still printed what it could; the new code prints NOTHING (cat fails, `|| true`).
findings.correction: After assembly: `[ -s "$blk" ] || echo "${pfx}diagnostics unavailable: could not write $blk" >&2` (one line < PIPE_BUF, atomic), then call the emitter only when the file exists. Same for the host block. The `|| true` / `return 0` contract and every `test_parallel_diag_t` timeout stay.

findings.where: mutants M2, M4, plus missing mutants
findings.defect: M2 (variable + printf) is declared non-killable; it IS killable deterministically by observing HOW the block is emitted, not by racing the write split. Also no mutant covers 'forgot rm -f of the block file' or 'lock left behind'.
findings.correction: Add a `cat` PATH shim (same gating/pass-through pattern as G4, env STUB_LOG) that logs `cat <args>` and execs the real cat; assert exactly 4 logged invocations whose argument matches `diag-block-<n>.txt` (3) / `diag-host-block.txt` (1), argument order `-- <file>`. M2 (printf of a variable), `echo "$(cat f)"`, and while-read re-emission then produce 0 matches => RED deterministically. Add post-run leak assertions on the preserved tmp tree (exit 1 preserves it): no `diag-block-*.txt`, no `diag-host-block.txt`, no `diag-emit.lock` directory remain (kills 'dropped rm -f' and M4 independently of the rmdir log). Add mutant M9 'drop rm -f' and M10 'release lock unconditionally (no got check)' (M10 is behaviourally equivalent: record as accepted, killed only by the code comment/review).

findings.defect: States 'On Linux pipe_write holds the pipe mutex for the whole write unless the 64 KB pipe is full' as if guaranteed; the task requires an explicit guarantee statement. Also 'lock makes emits mutually exclusive' omits that the 3 s fall-through and non-lock writers (WARNING echo, bash job-control notices from `set -m`) are outside it.
findings.correction: Replace with the three-part statement recorded in result.independent_verification.atomicity_statement_required_in_design and copy it verbatim into the script comment above test_parallel_diag_emit (primary = single write(2) + free pipe space; secondary = lock for cooperating emitters; known residual = stalled reader > 3 s, or a WARNING/job-control line landing at a page boundary when the pipe is full; neither occurs in the harness, whose reader is `cat`). Test assertion (c) must therefore not claim more than 'no foreign line inside while the pipe has space'.

findings.defect: M5 (unbounded lock loop) with an always-denying mkdir shim spins forever: run_until_premise then escalates through 3 attempts (~40 s each) and Port.close does not kill the bash tree, leaving orphan bash/sleep loops on the host. Baseline loop uses `--only line:<n>`; the standard, line-shift-safe form is `file.exs:LINE`.
findings.correction: In the mutant procedure add: after M5 (and any :timeout), `pkill -f letflow_test_parallel` / kill every `sleep 0.1` loop and the stub `sleep 600`s; verify `ps` clean before the next mutant. Baseline: `mix test test/scripts/test_parallel_watchdog_diag_test.exs:<line of the huge test on UNMODIFIED main> --repeat-until-failure 10` (Elixir 1.20.3 per .tool-versions supports it), chunk loop as designed, N=40 baseline / N=50 fixed, and the baseline handoff must treat 'no reproduction on the Windows host' as expected (not a defect, not a pass of the fix); acceptance of the fix rests on T1..T3 + mutant RED + container numbers.

findings.defect: started_at 2026-10-13T03:05:00Z is AFTER completed_at 2026-10-13T02:59:33Z (and after the wall clock at validation time, 03:04:59Z). core-directives 'completed_at must never precede started_at'.
findings.correction: ORCH (not the validator) sets step-01 started_at to a clock value <= completed_at (e.g. 02:55:00Z) in the next ORCH bookkeeping commit; run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir` on it.

passed_checks: Root cause and offsets re-derived from raw CI log of job 114960028887 (4096 = 12*336 + 64).
Third job (115074477292) text not re-fetched: the first two suffice for the same signature; the issue-fixer also recorded it as absent.
Temp-file + single cat is the correct fix direction; variable+printf and sed -u rejected correctly (stdio splits >4 KB; whole-line interleave remains).
EXIT-trap BASHPID guard unaffected: the helper adds no trap and only removes its own `$tmp_dir/diag-*` files; tmp_dir rm -rf stays main-shell only.
diag-host.lock (mkdir, never released, one winner) and diag-emit.lock are distinct names; a nested/other runner invocation has its own mktemp -d tmp_dir, so no sharing.
No errexit anywhere (only `set -u`): release-on-error concern reduces to G1 plus TERM/SIGKILL stale-lock, handled by the iteration-bounded fall-through.
TEST_PARALLEL_PARTITION_TIMEOUT_S semantics untouched; added latency on the normal path is one cat + rm (<1 ms); stale-lock worst case bounded by G5.

Other concurrent stderr emitters: only the watchdog WARNING echos (one line, < PIPE_BUF) and bash job-control notices (one write each) land between blocks; Step 3/4 summaries run in the main shell after the watchdogs are done. No additional multi-line concurrent emitter found (create-N.log, sampler, partition logs are files).
Baseline statistics 0.94^N correct; mutex discipline and ~40 min cap acceptable once G10 applied.
result.reroute: CODE-DESIGNER (or ISSUE-FIXER amendment) applies G1..G10 to the design in a new handoff, then CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gates. G11 is an ORCH bookkeeping edit. No part of the diagnosis needs redoing.
